chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: Omaha territory bands: Lloyd Hunter and trumpeter Irving Randolph
summary: Omaha had many territory bands with buses; Irving 'Mouse' Randolph came from Lloyd Hunter's band into Fletcher's.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: There used to be quite a few territory bands out of Omaha, and a number of them did have buses that way.

Yes. There was another bandleader there named Lloyd Hunter that had a great band, man. There was a trumpet player there -- there is a trumpet player, rather -- I think he's still living in New York City -- he joined Fletcher's band from this particular outfit, and his name is Irving Randolph. I don't know if you ever heard of him.

Terrific trumpet player. He could read. He could play. He went to New York and he made real good. He really did a good job in bands. They nicknamed him Mouse. He looked like a little mouse, but he could play. He came out of one of the Omaha bands.
